title: Dance bands of the 1920s and Homestead's local bands
summary: They discuss dance bands of the era and the Homestead band her uncle led, and a Whiteman-style concert.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I imagine Paul Whiteman's band would have been about that size and had the same number of pieces.
Well, he had a full brass section -- it was a regular dance band. I imagine besides the things that he might have arranged, he probably played a lot of --
But there weren't regular dance bands in the 1920s, I don't think.

Oh, yeah, there were quite a few dance bands. I remember when I was quite young in Homestead that bands used to come through Homestead, The Lloyd Brothers which was a very popular band in those days and Cecil Scott's band. All these bands played -- there were big bands and you had bands that played in the pits, especially in the theaters where they had the black productions and there was a field for musicians, quite a few. The only way I would know, I wouldn't know about Cliff's band and I wouldn't know about what was happening in New York. But around Pittsburgh, Homestead where I come from, there were quite a lot of musicians and a lot of bands that

played the local dances and I had an uncle who led The Homestead Band, you know, in fact he played tenor and he taught, too. He knew all the instruments. And they played the local concerts, the jazz concerts. There was definitely a field -- we've got a lot of musicians -- there's a lot of musicians that are no longer with us, but I'm sure they could tell you a lot of things about what they did and the music in their earlier days.

I think when Cliff had his band, along with the stuff that he arranged, he also probably played a lot of stock arrangements because they had to have quite a repertoire. There was a lot of dancing in those days. You'd go to a dance and the band would strike up and these were the days when ballroom dancing was very popular and they would have to have quite a repertoire, they played waltzes and every time a new dance would come up -- fox trot, you know, these were the days.
So there were plenty of bands around.
Uh-huh. There was a string section?
